Uncovering Tor users: where anonymity ends in the Darknet

Most of these are known attacks, but a good article nonetheless.

Some of these attacks are the reason why Whonix is such a valuable project. Things like the flash + javascript attacks are not as "Effective" since any good attack would have to bypass your Virtualization software, and also beat the Whonix Gateway + Desktop model. Although it's just as likely to be exploited, it still contains the attack to prevent disclosure of your true IP.

The other issue is just keeping up with updates. The HTML5 attacks listed in the article are avoidable since the Tor Browser prompts you about anyway sites that attempt to access canvas data.

As for regular attacks on correlation and whatnot, thats a bit more difficult. If you use your own Tor Entry point, it prevents your ISP (for the most part) from knowing you are using Tor. Mainly because it looks just like any other secure connection.
A Tor user using Flash is just asking to be attacked.
